design_summary: Synthesizable FPGA control shell for an external aerodynamic surrogate service. The RTL performs request capture, compact transaction sequencing, bounded queueing, response validation, watchdog supervision, CSR/MMIO control and status reporting, and bounded actuator-command generation. It does not implement aerodynamics or any surrogate model; it only manages transport, validation, safety, and firmware-visible control-plane behavior.

fixed_assumptions: Single synchronous clock domain on clk.

Top-level model transport follows the mandatory direction contract: model-request valid/data are outputs and model-request ready is an input; model-response valid/data are inputs and model-response ready is an output.
Exactly one outstanding transaction is supported by default; a small bounded queue depth may be enabled by CSR.
CSR/MMIO uses a compact 64-bit register window and is firmware-visible.
No bulk surrogate tensors, pressure fields, or flow fields are exposed at the top level.
On invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, actuator output validity is deasserted and faults are latched for software handling; no silent substitute command is generated.

top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level adaptive aerodynamics control shell. Implements top-level request/response transport, compact CSR/MMIO decode, request staging into a bounded FIFO, sequence tagging, watchdog supervision, response validation, and bounded actuator command outputs. The top module owns the externally visible streaming and firmware-visible interfaces.
top_module.functionality: Top-level shell for adaptive aerodynamic command transport. Accepts firmware CSR writes and reads, captures incoming request packets, extracts compact request fields, maintains a bounded request FIFO in technology-neutral FPGA-friendly inferred memory, tags and tracks the active sequence, emits a compact model request over the external transport path, accepts and validates the returned model response, supervises a programmable watchdog, and derives bounded actuator command outputs only from validated response metadata and CSR limit settings. On reset and on any invalid, stale, timeout, or protocol-fault condition, the module deasserts actuator output validity and preserves sticky fault indicators for firmware inspection. The module exposes explicit firmware-visible control, status, and observability registers through the CSR/MMIO interface.
responsibilities: Implement a synthesizable top-level FPGA control shell with real streaming request/response transport and real CSR/MMIO access.
Decode and expose firmware-visible control bits and numeric fields via the 64-bit CSR window.
Capture and compactly store request packets in bounded FPGA-friendly memory.
Maintain exactly one outstanding request by default and optionally a small bounded queue when enabled by CSR.
Generate and validate monotonic sequence tags for requests and responses.
Start and stop the watchdog around outstanding transactions.
Clamp actuator commands to configured min/max bounds and optionally rate-limit them.
Inhibit actuator validity on reset, timeout, stale response, malformed response, force-inhibit, or protocol error.
Expose status and counters for software observability.
Drive all externally visible outputs with real RTL logic; no top-level output may be left without a driver.
top_module.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, initialize the FSM to IDLE, clear outstanding sequence tracking, clear FIFO pointers, reset the watchdog and counters, clear sticky status bits, deassert m_axis_act_valid and m_axis_resp_valid, and place the design into an inhibited state with no actuator command validity asserted.
behavior_rules: The top-level FSM shall include at least IDLE, ISSUE_REQ, WAIT_RESP, VALIDATE_RESP, APPLY_CMD, and a fault/inhibit handling state implemented as deterministic synchronous state transitions.
Requests are accepted only when s_axis_req_valid and s_axis_req_ready are both high.
Each accepted request shall be compacted into request record fields including sequence number, control mode, geometry token, and flow-condition fields.
The model request transport shall use model_req_valid/model_req_data as outputs and model_req_ready as an input.
The model response transport shall use model_rsp_valid/model_rsp_data as inputs and model_rsp_ready as an output.
A response is valid only when the response sequence matches the active outstanding sequence and the response is flagged complete and fresh.
Invalid, stale, malformed, or timed-out responses shall be discarded and shall not alter actuator outputs.
Actuator command outputs shall be derived only from validated response metadata and CSR limit settings, then clamped to configured min/max bounds before m_axis_act_valid is asserted.

If no valid response is available, if force inhibit is asserted, if enable is deasserted, or if a fault exists, actuator validity shall remain deasserted and the command shall not be silently substituted as a valid new command.
Timeout threshold shall be programmable via cfg_timeout_cycles and shall default to a safe reset value.
Status counters may saturate.
The request FIFO is technology-neutral and may be mapped to FPGA block RAM in implementation.
No bulk payload, tensor, pressure, or flow field shall be exposed as a top-level pin.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_req_fifo_wrapper
modules.description: Technology-neutral FIFO wrapper for compact request records. Intended to map to native FPGA inferred block RAM or distributed RAM while preserving a small bounded storage structure. It stores only compact request records and does not materialize model payloads or large history arrays.
modules.functionality: Implements a bounded, FPGA-friendly request buffer for compact control records only. Exposes push/pop handshakes and queue occupancy. Uses inferred-memory style storage suitable for native FPGA block RAM mapping. The wrapper is not a model, not a fallback controller, and not a substitute command generator.
responsibilities: Provide bounded FIFO storage for compact request records.
Expose simple push/pop semantics to the top-level control FSM.
Use technology-neutral inferred memory behavior suitable for FPGA inference.
Avoid any inference of ASIC-only hard macros or large register arrays.
Keep request buffering compact and bounded.
Receive a real memory readback input from the FIFO storage datapath to close the inferred memory interface.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset clears queue state, deasserts ready/valid outputs as appropriate, and leaves the buffer empty.
behavior_rules: Storage shall remain bounded to the declared depth.
Only compact request records are stored.
The wrapper shall not expose or compute surrogate model data.
FIFO control shall remain fully synthesizable and deterministic.
The storage implementation shall be technology-neutral and suitable for FPGA inference rather than hard macro instantiation.
mem_dout is a consumer-side readback input from the inferred memory datapath and must be structurally driven by the parent design.
The module shall not invent surrogate payload semantics for memory readback.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_csr_decode
modules.description: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO decoder for the compact 64-bit register window. It translates bus transactions into explicit semantic control outputs and produces readable status and configuration fields for the top-level control shell.
modules.functionality: Implements a compact CSR/MMIO window with explicit semantic configuration fields and status fields. Supports firmware writes to control enable, clear faults, force inhibit, queue depth enable, response-accept enable, timeout cycles, actuator clamp limits, and rate limit step. Supports reads of live status and counters. The decoder shall expose only reachable, implemented registers and shall not claim inaccessible internal state as software-visible.
responsibilities: Decode the 64-bit firmware-visible register window.
Produce explicit control outputs for the top-level controller.
Provide readable status and counters to software.
Guarantee that every declared register in the contract is reachable by RTL decode.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset returns all control bits to safe defaults and the read-data path to a benign value. Sticky fault-clearing requires explicit firmware write after reset if implemented as write-one-to-clear semantics.
behavior_rules: Every declared register must be implemented in the RTL decode path.
No register may be listed as software-visible unless it is reachable through decode.
Status fields shall reflect live controller state and saturating counters.
The decoder is purely digital and synthesizable.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_transport_ctrl
modules.description: Synchronous controller for request issue, model-response acceptance, timeout supervision, validation, and actuator command derivation. It owns the top-level FSM and the bounded command path, but it does not compute aerodynamics or provide any substitute fallback command. On fault or invalid conditions it inhibits actuator validity and latches status for firmware handling.
modules.functionality: Implements the deterministic FSM and control policy for request acceptance, request issuance, response validation, timeout supervision, command clamping, and inhibit-only fault handling. Derives actuator command validity only from validated response metadata and configuration limits. Maintains sticky faults and status counters. The controller is required to inhibit outputs on reset, timeout, stale data, malformed responses, protocol errors, and force-inhibit conditions; it shall not generate a substitute fallback command.
responsibilities: Implement the FSM states IDLE, ISSUE_REQ, WAIT_RESP, VALIDATE_RESP, APPLY_CMD, and a deterministic fault/inhibit path.
Sequence and track at most one outstanding transaction by default unless queueing is enabled.
Validate response sequence and freshness metadata against the active outstanding request.
Supervise timeout cycles and set sticky timeout fault on expiry.
Clamp commanded outputs to configured min/max and optional rate-limit step.
Deassert actuator validity on any invalid condition.
Expose status and observability counters.
Consume explicit model request/response handshake signals from the top-level transport path.
Consume response record fields provided by the response-formatting path rather than inventing them internally.
Consume raw command payload and validity from the command-generation path for clamping and output qualification.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset forces IDLE, clears outstanding state and watchdog state, clears sequence trackers and counters, deasserts all valid outputs, and leaves the controller in a safe inhibited condition with no actuator command validity asserted.
behavior_rules: All transitions shall be deterministic and synchronous.
A response is accepted only if response acceptance is enabled, the sequence matches, the response is complete, and freshness is valid.
Timeout shall begin when a request is accepted and stop on validated response acceptance.
Sticky faults shall remain asserted until explicitly cleared through CSR if such clear semantics are implemented.
On any fault or invalid condition, only inhibit behavior is allowed; no substitute command may be silently generated.
model_req_ready and model_rsp_valid/model_rsp_data are explicit transport inputs from the external model-side interface.
resp_record_* and cmd_raw_* are explicit internal path inputs produced by the response-packaging and command-generation logic within the same hierarchy.
